idiom_name: typed query module over pg's Pool (row interfaces)
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds only compile-time types on top of the JavaScript drivers, so the gateway is a module of functions over pg's Pool with one parameterized statement per function and an interface per row - the direct analogue of the catalog pattern, with SQL visible in one module per table. Choose it when the SQL is hand-tuned or vendor-specific and when the team prefers statements over builders; the weakness is that the row interface is asserted, not checked.
pitfalls: Row interfaces are erased at runtime: a column rename breaks callers with no compile error.
pg returns numeric/bigint columns as strings by default, so a `number` field can be wrong at runtime until type parsers are configured.
One Pool per process: constructing a pool inside a gateway factory multiplies server connections.

variants.name: Kysely typed query builder over a Database interface
variants.implementation_notes: Kysely makes the schema the type: a Database interface (usually generated with kysely-codegen) names every table and column, and the builder only accepts what is declared - db.selectFrom('user').select(['id','name']).where('id','=',id).executeTakeFirst() returns a typed row. Use it when the schema is stable and composition or compile-time safety matters more than seeing the SQL; keep the raw sql`` template for statements the builder cannot express, and thread transactions by passing the Transaction object explicitly.
pitfalls: The Database interface must be regenerated when the schema changes, or it silently drifts and the compile-time guarantee is a lie.
A gateway that closes over the root db cannot be enlisted in a transaction; pass the Transaction object through.
Builder-generated SQL hides the actual statement from review - explain/EXPLAIN is the only way to see what the database receives.
